---
title: Long guide
---
This guide exercises nested sections, repeated labels, long content, and responsive navigation. Return to the [overview](../../) or read the [code examples](../../reference/code-examples/).

## Plan the site

Write for the reader who is discovering the project for the first time. A good introduction describes the outcome, the prerequisites, and the next useful step. Keep paragraphs focused so that they remain readable on a narrow screen.

### First steps

- Identify the reader and the task.
- Explain the expected result.
  - Include a concrete example.
  - Link to the reference when detail is needed.

### Configure `site.title`

Use a recognizable title and clear navigation labels. Inline code remains literal, including `<script>not executable</script>`.

## Build the content

A documentation page combines explanation with examples. Prefer a direct statement followed by evidence. Tables should scroll locally on small displays instead of widening the entire page.

| Stage | Input | Result | Responsibility |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Writing | Plain Markdown documents and referenced image assets | Reviewable source content | Documentation authors |
| Building | The configured consumer site and installed standalone theme | Static HTML, CSS, and JavaScript assets | The existing Jigyll build command |
| Reading | Published static files served at the configured hosting root | Accessible documentation and working navigation | The browser |

### First steps

This repeated heading must navigate to its own emitted identifier. No theme-generated slug should replace the renderer's identifier.

> Verify the output a reader sees. A successful build alone cannot establish interaction or visual parity.

## Review the structure

A useful document has a stable structure and clear transitions. Each section should answer one question, explain any important constraints, and point toward the next action. The same source should be readable on a phone, an intermediate display, and a desktop monitor.

### Practical details

1. Read the page from beginning to end.
2. Follow each link using the keyboard.
3. Check the examples without changing their whitespace.

Keep the result straightforward. Long-lived documentation benefits from precise terminology, ordinary links, and examples that can be copied without editing. Repeated checks catch stale assumptions before they become confusing instructions.
